decisions.executionNote: Begin left-arm elbow-up approach; mallet lies near center with handle on the left. Raise and gradually rotate for a top-down handle grasp.
Translate toward the left end of the handle while completing most of the downward wrist rotation; right arm stays parked.
Align open left fingers across the shaft near its left end, stopping above the estimated grasp height.
Use wrist view to center the handle between the fingers and lower the link6 pose to grasp height.
Make a small lateral centering correction and close the left gripper around the mallet shaft.
Lift the closed grasp to verify retention, moving left and turning the mallet toward the xylophone above table clearance.
Mallet is visibly retained. Sweep its head forward at clearance and bring the left wrist toward the first red key.
Finish pointing the mallet forward and descend toward the first red key. Contact height remains visually estimated.
Tap the first red key, then lift more than 0.025 m before beginning the move toward the orange key.
Move the raised mallet to the second, orange key and make a vertical tap, then begin lifting.
Lift clear after the orange tap, advance to the yellow key while raised, and start its vertical descent.
Tap yellow, lift safely, then begin aligning for green. Slightly turn the mallet right so the left wrist can stay in its own workspace for later keys.
Finish aligning over green, make its vertical strike, and start the post-hit lift while retaining the mallet.
Complete green's lift, move the raised tip to light blue, and begin its descent. Keep the left wrist left of center.
Strike the light-blue key and lift 0.045 m, then position the raised tip over dark blue with the wrist still on the left.
Visually refine dark-blue alignment, tap vertically, and lift before moving to the purple key.
Increase the post-strike clearance to account for the link6-to-mallet offset, then aim at purple without crossing the left wrist into the right workspace.
Strike purple from the visually aligned position and lift with a generous clearance before the last key.
Lift farther, align the mallet over the rightmost magenta key using wrist yaw, and descend for the final tap.
Replan after the continuity rejection: smaller coupled lowering and alignment increments, then a controlled vertical tap on the last key.
Complete the rightmost-key contact and lift the mallet well clear, allowing observation of whether the full sequence has registered.
The episode has not ended; earlier lifts may have been too small at the actual mallet tip. Return above the leftmost key to repeat with larger verified clearance.
Continue returning above red while maintaining a higher mallet clearance; use a forward-pointing orientation for the new left-to-right pass.
Restart on red with its center aligned under the tip. Use a full downward tap followed by a substantially larger lift.
Correct the rejected tensor without compensating for motion: complete the red lift, advance to orange at clearance, and descend.
Center the tip on orange, complete its downward tap, then lift 0.08 m with no lateral motion.
Advance at full clearance from orange to yellow, then strike straight down with the mallet tip.
Correct the rejected tensor from the unchanged pose: lift after yellow, then advance to green with the right arm stationary.
Strike green vertically and begin the generous post-hit lift; the shaft remains visibly held.
Complete the high lift after green, translate above light blue, and begin a straight downward stroke.
Complete the light-blue strike and raise the mallet by 0.08 m before proceeding right.
Move the raised mallet from light blue to dark blue using a small yaw change, keeping the wrist left of center, then descend.
Complete the dark-blue tap and lift straight up by 0.08 m, preserving the grasp and elbow-up configuration.
Align the raised tip over purple using a modest yaw change, then lower vertically for the seventh strike.
Finish the purple contact slightly farther inside the bar, then lift 0.075 m before proceeding to the final magenta key.
Position the raised mallet over the rightmost magenta bar, keeping the left wrist left of center, and deliver the final downward tap.
